summary: Pure restatement: 1/a+1/b+1/c = 4/n with weights as denominators is the ES equation itself; the Fano/well-formedness conditions are inequalities and gcd conditions that do not produce this equality.
Meta/category item: the group-law 'sum' of points is undefined and the item itself records a category error, so there is no testable ES content.

Log-CY structure of the ES cubic (projective closure = Cayley cubic, boundary triangle, S4 on nodes, ES(n) <=> integral point with y3=-n) is already PROVED in the cayley memo; the torsor/cluster identification is the open part.

Computed the Z[sqrt2] cone test (x and conjugate x' both in [1,B]) with exact arithmetic: at B=80 for the 21 primes p≡1 mod 4 up to 200, Z-only triples cover 2 primes and the full cone covers 5 (4 with genuinely irrational elements). The bounded search finds no mechanism; larger B would need a smarter search.

Value-set/cover reformulation is definitional (Type II families are covers of the p-line); the Hilbert-irreducibility and thin-set value-set theory that would supply density statements is the framework already catalogued in the repo.

Literature check: arXiv searches for Egyptian fractions with linear forms in logarithms returned no hits; a web search finds only the general Baker theory (Waldschmidt, Baker 1975). No ES statement with an explicit linear form in logs is identified, so the 'forcing' step has no target.

Pell test: for each p≡1 mod 4 up to 1500 (116 primes), the minimal solution of x²−py²=−1 gives candidate denominators {x±1, y, 2y, 4y, (x±1)/2, (x±1)/4}. Certificates using such a denominator exist for 4 primes, versus 8 for a shifted control set, so the Legendre-type candidate has no advantage.

Non-scaled certificates of 4/(pq) counted as U(pq)−U(p)−U(q) (scaled ones are exactly the U(p) and U(q) solutions): for p≤59 and q<200 the count grows with p and q (p=53: mean 406 over q). It tracks U(p) on the 7 primes tested (Spearman 0.93, too few points to mean much); the R(p) correlation was not run.

Already computed: classical_corr.json gives U(p) vs a_p(11a1)/2sqrt p +0.0034, a_p(37a1) -0.0021, |a_p(32a)|/2sqrt p +0.0089, tau(p)/p^5.5 +0.0013 (item quoted -0.005, +0.007, +0.006 — numbers slightly off).
minz(p) = 0 mod p for p<=2e5 is covered: the repo's fingerprint item 0190 gives the lemma x|z <=> y|z (which forces p|z), and variants2.json records x|z failing only at 2521.

The sequence and its correlation are in the repo: classical_corr.json gives minz(p)/p vs tau(4p+1) = -0.421 (item -0.42); the R(p) correlation (-0.31) and the identification with least C remain untested.

Windows at 2·10⁵, 10⁶ and 10⁷ from the repo's count program (minz column): max log minz/log p = 1.83, 1.73, 1.63 (small samples), max minz/p² falls 0.136 → 0.025 → 0.0024, median minz/p grows 481 → 1660 → 6178 (about p^0.6), and minz is a multiple of p in every case.
Correlation of U(p) with log P+(p-1)/log p (+0.3965, item +0.40) is already in classical_corr.json; the Baker-Harman density split of 'ES-hard' among smooth p-1 is not yet done.

summary: Greedy numerator potential: x1 = ceil(p/4) always leaves numerator 4x1−p = 3 for p≡1 mod 4, so the Sylvester-type potential never decreases. The 2-term step for 3/(p·x1) fails at 19 of 147 primes ≤2000 (73, 193, 241, 313, 409, 433, 601, 673, …).

Union–find over primes (p<3000) and witness templates (C,d), C≤12, with an edge when d|4Cp+1 and d≡−1 mod 4C: the giant component holds 207 of 211 primes. This is trivial, since each template is a residue class of p mod d, so the merging carries no extra information.

Involutions of the cubic surface through rational points (Vieta/Markoff moves) and their positivity behaviour are already analysed (the orbit argument shows Markoff moves preserve positivity but are sparse).
Pure restatement: the total space of n = 4xyz/(xy+yz+zx) is rational because n is an explicit rational function on A³; the value-set question is ES itself.

Arxiv 1406.6963 (Y. Wang, verified) proves density of rational points on Cayley's cubic with coordinates of few prime factors via circle method plus universal torsors. The 'saturation' title in the item is misleading; the relevant object is the ES cubic (Cayley cubic, cayley memo P1), so the result may give almost-prime rational points that could be steered to a fixed fibre n=p or a congruence class of a coordinate.
next: Read Wang's main theorem; decide whether its almost-prime count survives restriction to the fibre y3=-p (or to a residue class of one coordinate); if yes, this is a route to few-prime denominators in ES.

Not run: the Hermitian Z-module model of (u,C) needs an explicit lattice and Gram matrix, then successive minima for p≤10⁴. Estimate >1 h of modelling and coding.

summary: Candidate induction maps on the 9 no-witness primes (C≤30): (p+3)/4 gives 103, 145, 1090, …; (p−1)/4 gives 102, 144, …; the largest prime factor of p+3 gives 103, 29, 109, …. None of the images is a no-witness prime, so these maps show no closure.
Pure restatement/tautology: if q divides every denominator of a solution of 4/(pq), dividing by q gives a solution of 4/p, so the descending solutions are exactly the scaled ones.

Abstract of arXiv:1901.08503 (Wilsch) checked: it counts integral points of bounded height on a blow-up of P^3 outside planes via universal torsors, not a log Fano threefold like U_n. The stated comparison therefore does not apply directly.

Literature check (arXiv 1601.07066, Corvaja–Zannier review): the Hilbert property is set against the Chevalley–Weil theorem and linked to simply connected varieties, with Enriques-surface counterexamples. It gives no thin-image statement for the ES fibration n: X → A¹, so the Mordell–Schinzel analogy stays heuristic.

Literature check: Tian (arXiv 1210.8231) and Tian–Yuan (1411.4728) prove congruent-number rank results via Heegner points and 2-Selmer parity. ES has no Selmer analogue, so the input does not transfer.

Literature check: Smith (arXiv 1603.08479, existence checked) proves positive density of congruent numbers from 2-Selmer distributions. The method needs a family of elliptic curves with a Selmer group, and ES has none, so nothing transfers.

Arxiv 2504.10992 (Dao) checked: Markoff-type K3 surfaces with Zariski-dense rational points but integral Hasse failure due to Brauer–Manin. Bright–Loughran say BM is absent for ES, so the mechanism does not transfer.

Same source as Z2114 (arXiv 2504.10992, abstract checked): integral Hasse failure despite Zariski-dense rational points, via Brauer–Manin. The local-test audit cannot be done from the abstract alone, and BM is absent for ES (Bright–Loughran), so no transfer is established.
Same source as Z2114 (arXiv 2504.10992): the audit of local tests needs the full paper, which was not read. From the abstract, the failing mechanism is BM, which Bright–Loughran say is absent for ES.

Kronecker–Hurwitz identity Σ_t H(4n−t²) = 2σ(n) − Σ_{d|n} min(d,n/d) verified numerically for n≤12 with a reduced-form class-number count (weights 1/2, 1/3, H(0)=−1/12). The Type I sums Σ_c H(p²+4c²d) vary the discriminant with c and are not of this fixed-n shape, so no trace identity for ES is found.

Count test: f(l*p)/f(p) for l=2,3,5,7 over primes p≡1 mod 4 up to 200 gives mean 4.6, 12.1, 10.8, 25.7 with sd about 1/3 to 1/2 of the mean (range 2.7–9.5 for l=2), so no Hecke-type constant relation. Multiplicativity fails as expected.

Literature check (Bringmann–Manschot et al. exact formulas, arXiv 1006.0915 and related, existence checked) and growth check: R(n) is polylogarithmic, while mock forms of negative weight have coefficients of exponential growth. Weight-1 shapes were not tested.

Literature check: Pilatte (arXiv 2310.19357, existence checked) builds a divisibility graph on integers; replacing the vertex set by {4Cp+1} needs a spec that the item does not give, so no test was possible from the text.

Computed normalised spectral gaps of Cayley graphs of (Z/4C)* generated by the distinct prime factors of 4Cp+1 (C≤5, p≲1000). The gap is 0 for some primes (disconnected generators) and the mean is large for C=1 (tiny group), so the generated graphs are often not expanders.

Second-moment check over levels at fixed p (witness counts D_C(p), 1124 primes p≤2·10⁴, C≤30): level variance over mean is 2.51, so the level counts are over-dispersed relative to Poisson. The shifted-convolution route (Blomer–Harcos, math/0703246) was not carried out in full.

Test of Hecke-type relations: the ratios f(l*p)/f(p) (l=2,3,5,7) are not constant across p (2.7–9.5 for l=2), so no linear Hecke relation with fixed coefficients is visible among f(p), f(lp), f(l^2p) in the tested range.

OAI 178 excerpt read (sources/oai2026/178-excerpts.md, CLAIMED): deterministic Ramanujan-graph constructions. At the sizes used here (C≤30) the sampling cost is negligible, so explicit expanders give no measurable gain for ES searches.

Murmuration-style test on U(p)/log²p (primes ≤3·10⁴): bin means rise 0.83, 0.94, 1.00, 1.06 across p-windows, and class means mod 840 range from 0.43 (classes 1, 121, 361: Mordell's hard classes) to 1.70 (class 557). The structure is the known class effect, with no separate oscillation.
Parity of ES counts (complement pairing) and the mod-2 structure are analysed in PARITY_FIXED_P.md.

Literature check (Radchenko–Viazovska arXiv 1701.00265, existence checked): interpolation formulas apply to Schwartz functions with modular data. ES counts are not coefficients of a lattice theta series (none identified), and their polylog growth does not match the functions in that theory.

Literature check (Bruinier–Funke math/0212286, abstract checked): theta lifts for O(p,2) with cycles and Borcherds lifts. No ES generating function with the required principal part is identified, and polylog growth of counts is not what those lifts produce.

Shape distribution of all certificates (p<1000): 50 hard-prime certificates vs 2028 others. Mean log_p z is 2.22 (hard) vs 2.22 (others), and the fraction with z>p^1.8 is 0.90 vs 0.86. No escape of mass to extreme shapes is visible in this range.

Reasoning check: the level-t series are Eisenstein plus theta-quotient pieces (METAPLECTIC_ES.md), so there is no cusp component whose vanishing would force a level-lowering contradiction. No explicit space is defined by the item.

Divisor-lattice depth via the witness pipeline (p≤2·10⁴, C≤30): for the 3894 witnessing pairs the minimal number of prime factors Ω reaching −1 is 1 for 2799, 2 for 971, 3 for 117, 4 for 7. One prime-factor step usually suffices.

Subset-product reachability (DP over prime factors): the mean fraction of unit residues mod 4C reached by divisors is 0.728 for witnessing pairs and 0.221 for non-witnessing pairs (p≤2·10⁴, C≤30). Reach predicts the witness well.

Shortest zero-sum-type witness: the minimal number of factors (with multiplicity) whose product is ≡ −1 mod 4C has the same histogram as Ω (1: 2799, 2: 971, 3: 117, 4: 7), with maximum 4 in this range.
Minimal sufficient factor multisets: in the witness data the minimal number of prime factors reaching −1 is at most 4 (p≤2·10⁴, C≤30), and one factor suffices in 72% of witnessing pairs.

Additive energy of log-residue sets needs cyclic (Z/4C)*, which holds only for 4C=4 among C≤30 (e.g. (Z/20)* ≅ Z2×Z4). The energy test is therefore vacuous for all but C=1, and that case has group order 2.

Persistence of witnesses from C to C+1 (p≤2·10⁴): P(W(C+1)|W(C)) is 0.379 for C=1→2, below the base rate 0.442 at C=2; the persistence falls with C. Witnesses are anti-persistent across adjacent levels.
Witness hypergraph (edges = sets of C-levels witnessing each prime, p≤2·10⁴): the greedy transversal needs 14 C-levels to hit every prime.

summary: Separation done: among 33720 (p,C) pairs (p<=2e4, C<=30), 23350 have −1 outside the generated subgroup, 6476 have −1 in it without a divisor witness, 3894 have a witness; the subgroup test is not the binding constraint.

The e-slice count is a sum over divisor pairs of N=4Cp+1 with a congruence; the matrix is a circulant on (Z/e)*, not a planar graph. No determinant formula is identified; the Pfaffian route needs planarity, which fails here.

Run to p≤2·10⁴: the longest run of consecutive primes ≡1 mod 24 with no C≤2 witness is 4 (primes 6841–7129). Extending to 10⁸ needs about 7·10⁵ primes with two factorisations each, minutes in C with Pollard rho, more in Python.
